claim.why_it_matters: Heading at the wrong level: 4.4.2 is a child of 4.4 SUBSCRIPTING (### in the markdown) and a sibling of 4.4.1 (####), but is rendered at ###, the same level as its parent.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 99 (II-15) shows the heading '4.4.2 Subscripting Using Index-Names' and the markdown carries it word for word as a heading, so nothing is missing and the kind 'missing-heading' is wrong. The rest of the page's prose matches the markdown. The PDF prints every numbered heading in the same plain style and has no heading depth, so the page cannot show any discrepancy in level. The claim is only about markdown heading depth, which is formatting and changes no meaning. The levels are inconsistent across the section: 4.4 is ###, 4.4.1 is ####, and both 4.4.2 and 4.4.3 are ###. That suggests the outlier is 4.4.1, not 4.4.2. In any case it is markdown-hierarchy hygiene, not a content discrepancy against the PDF.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The heading is present, with identical text. The only issue is markdown heading depth in section 4.4 of the 1985 transcription: 4.4.1 is at #### while its siblings 4.4.2 and 4.4.3 are at ###, the same depth as their parent 4.4. This is a formatting tidy-up, not a defect against the PDF.
